what_happened: The job raised the agent ceiling to 16, added recording of plan-group sizes, and fixed the stale help text. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One criterion was unmet: running `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` from the repo root, all passing. One check failed: the test check. Its recorded output is only CI checkout cleanup and a Node.js 20 deprecation warning, so it shows no test name or assertion. There were two major findings and no blocker. (1) Behavior criterion 9 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). (2) `group_sizes` records one entry per wave, not per plan group (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:2962-2979). On the one-at-a-time path (serial `drain()` and max_concurrency = 1, the default) it reports wrong sizes and a wrong group count.
cause: The request asked to record group sizes without saying what a group is on each drain path. The producer treated a wave as a group, which holds only when jobs run in parallel waves. Neither the criteria nor the tests required the recorded values to be checked on the serial path, which is the default and the most common one. The test-failure output kept in the event is CI cleanup noise, so the producer and the verifier could not see which test failed or why. Nothing required the criteria to be checked on every shipped mode, and the test check is judged only once, at the final verdict. This is the same late-verdict pattern as the earlier recording jobs, but the cause here is that one mode went untested.
prevention: For any job that adds recording or measurement to a flow with more than one mode, require one demonstration per criterion on each shipped mode. For drain that means serial `drain()`, max_concurrency = 1 and max_concurrency > 1, each checked against known inputs with the expected sizes and group count stated. Also change the failed-check capture to keep the failing test name and assertion, not CI cleanup text. Behavior criteria should require evidence from commands that ran (D43), which the producer runs and reports.
proposed_request:
Fix group-size recording in drain so it records one entry per plan group on every drain path. Outcome: after any drain, the recorded group sizes and group count match the plan's real groups whether the drain ran serially (`drain()`), with max_concurrency = 1 (the default), or with max_concurrency > 1. Keep the agent ceiling at 16 and the corrected `athena drain` help text from job 20261106-012852-h7de. Acceptance criteria:
- With a plan of known groups, for example sizes 3, 1 and 2, serial `drain()` records sizes [3,1,2] and a group count of 3.
- The same plan with max_concurrency = 1 records the same sizes and count.
- The same plan with max_concurrency > 1 records the same sizes and count.
- Each criterion has one demonstration, and its evidence cites the commands that ran.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass from the repo root, with the failing test name shown if any test fails.
Read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs around lines 2962-2979, where one entry is recorded per wave. The root cause to name is that a wave is not a plan group on the one-at-a-time path.
